hints: Count each distinct value once in every subarray containing it.
Assign a value?s contribution to its first occurrence inside a subarray.
For an occurrence, valid left endpoints start after its previous occurrence.
analogy: Each occurrence claims the subarrays where it is the first copy of its value.
example: For [1,2,1], the distinct counts are 1,1,1,2,2,2, summing to 9.
algorithm: Scan positions i=1..n and keep the previous position prev[x] of every value, initially zero. Add (i-prev[x])*(n-i+1) to the answer, then set prev[x]=i. Use 64-bit arithmetic and a map or coordinate compression.
correctness: The occurrence at i is the first copy of x in exactly the subarrays whose left endpoint is in prev[x]+1..i and right endpoint in i..n. These classes assign each value in each subarray to exactly one occurrence, so their total is the desired sum.
complexity: For n elements, a hash map gives expected O(n) time and O(n) space; sorting for compression gives O(n log n) time.
